meta.what: The Held in Human score read as data, so a picture of the piece can be drawn without re-reading it. Eight scenes, the events inside them, two channels that run the whole piece, the spoken lines with their silences, and the intro as the keystroke recording it is.

opacity.what: How much of the real room the visitor can see, as a step per scene with a ramp into each step.
opacity.unit: fraction of the general opacity level, 0 to 1
opacity.generalLevelNote: The master dimmer is at 1.0, so the per scene values are the real ones. The score warns that dimming reduces contrast and makes the picture dull.

lut.what: A colour lookup table on the passthrough image, as a step per scene with a ramp into each step.
lut.recommendation: use 0 if the previous scene has the same LUT

qanda.what: One voice, one cursor down one list, read by four scenes. An empty line is a silence of a stated length and is a real event.

model.what: The block holds one more line than the score asks for. Line 1 is the only one with a negative time and the only one that asks the visitor to do something, so it goes to the maze, which is the only scene with no duration and the only one that can wait. The score states how many lines each scene takes and never states which, so the assignment of EVERY line rests on this reading, not only the spare one.

evidence.what: line 1 is `-1` seconds, which is not a duration, and the maze is the only scene with no duration parameter
under this reading the last line spoken in the piece is `Yes, Let's go.`; under the alternative the score lists a line nobody ever says
the 46500 ms silence puts `Do you recognise it?` ending at 29500 ms into the outro and the outro text appears at 30000 ms, 500 ms later

model.alternative: the cursor starts at line 1, which puts the walk instruction inside the cylinder and leaves the last line unspoken

lines.text: Please walk towards the stairs in front of you.
Have you noticed how the walls don't meet the ceilings here?
Do you think thoughts wander in and out?
Do you remember what it was like to think freely?
Are you here?
Do you see me?
Things have changed here since yesterday, haven't they?
Did you notice the little leaf on the floor?
Did you touch it?
How long have we been here, do you think?
Will it end?
Does it matter?
Is the tree still here?
Do you recognise it?
Well? Shall we go?
Yes, Let's go.

keystrokes.what: The intro is not a string, it is a recording of somebody typing, with the pauses and one change of mind left in.
keystrokes.text:
When the piles for the university library foundations were
being driven in at night, the surrounding buildings would
shake. Hildegard soon got used to the earth quaking. As
readily as if she had been secretly longing for it all the time
and along with the longing for change had achieved an
altered state.

lines.text: /imagine being trapped in a loop of endless notifications.
/remember the silence that follows the storm.
/imagine disconnecting for just one day.
/remember the texture of real conversations.
/imagine all voices could be heard equally.
/remember when we used to meet face to face?
/imagine you could mute the world.
/remember to log off sometimes.
/imagine the art of missing out.
/remember the days before 'online' was a place.
/imagine a world where 'search' meant wandering in the woods.
/remember the feel of leaf between your fingers.
/imagine if every pixel carried a piece of the truth.
/remember these people are all acting.
/whisper the names of those forgotten by history.
/whisper the words that bring us closer in the dark.

outro.what: One paragraph, line breaks set by the author rather than wrapped.
outro.text:
I never looked at what kind of tree it was.
It didn’t have a species name, it was as if
I was more amazed by the will to live of a
tree as such rather than that of a birch or a
maple. Perhaps that’s how I look at people
too – the conditions are impossible yet the
person lives. Their name or where they’re
from seems secondary. It’s as if there’s
neither tree nor person if they don’t force
their way through rubble and circumstances.

credits.note: One group holds two roles, because the score separates that pair with a line break rather than the double break it uses everywhere else.

room.what: Where things stand. Every placement in the score has right = 0, so a placement here is a height, a distance and an angle.
room.axes: right, up, back, which is the score's own comment and is not Unity's frame

ambiguities.what: The credits begin at 7000 ms and scroll for 35000 ms, so they end at 42000 ms, which is 2000 ms past the scene's stated duration of 40000 ms. And `time after credits until intro` does not say which end of the credits it counts from.

readings.how: the wait runs from the end of the scroll, and the stated duration governs something else
the wait runs from the credits appearing, which puts the intro inside the stated duration
the credits are an overlay on their own clock and the scene is the stated duration
the scene ends when the scroll does

ambiguities.carriedAs: events[transition:credits].overrunsSceneMs is the 2 s, and order.entry holds both waits with their own durations

ambiguities.what: The only scene with no duration parameter, and the only QandA line with a negative time asks the visitor to walk towards the stairs. Nothing in the score says what ends it.

readings.how: the negative time holds until she walks

ambiguities.carriedAs: scenes[maze].durationMs is null and durationHow is `absent`

ambiguities.what: The block holds 24 lines and the score asks for 23. One line belongs to a scene the score gives no count for.

readings.how: line 1 belongs to the maze and the cursor runs down the rest in the order the score asks for them
the cursor starts at line 1, which puts the walk instruction inside the cylinder and leaves the last line unspoken

ambiguities.carriedAs: qanda.blocks[0].countHow is `inferred`, and EVERY line carries how: `inferred`, because the score counts lines per scene and never names them

ambiguities.what: The score's own recommendation is to use 0 if the previous scene has the same LUT. 2 scenes break it and they are adjacent: dialogue takes 0 ms into neutral to green, cylinder takes 5000 ms into the same LUT. Swapping the two fixes both.

readings.how: the fade list is off by one against the colour list
the hard cut into green arrives with the first spoken line and the 5 s is a harmless ramp between two identical tables

ambiguities.what: `LUT transition time transition` is 0 ms and the transition is neutral. The recommendation is satisfied only if the scene before it carries the same LUT, and the only candidate is the outro.

readings.how: the piece loops, and the transition is the reset between visitors

ambiguities.carriedAs: order.loops is true with how: `inferred`, and both channels take their first point's previous value from the last

ambiguities.what: 15 fragments in a 120000 ms scene, running from 1 word to 79, and the block carries no timing at all. The dialogue and the QandA both carry seconds per line.

readings.how: something outside the score paces them, or the sound design does, or they are run by hand

ambiguities.what: 4 entries carry a `;n,n` suffix using the values 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7. Nothing in the score says what they select.

readings.how: seven distinct values over an eight scene piece reads as which scenes the object is in
positions in maze.json, which the score does not hold

ambiguities.carriedAs: texts.mazeInner[].suffix is the parsed numbers and nothing is claimed about them

ambiguities.what: The last event is a space typed 10901 ms after the final full stop, which is the longest gap in the track.

readings.how: it is a keypress left in the recording

ambiguities.carriedAs: the last row of keystrokes.events, and keystrokes.longestGaps[0]

ambiguities.what: `r,a,d,i,s,h` is the only entry that spells a word out with commas.

readings.how: each letter is placed as its own object
a comma separated field that was never meant to be read as a word
